entries.title: Gajakesari Yoga
entries.body: Jupiter in a kendra (1st, 4th, 7th or 10th) from the Moon. The name joins the elephant and the lion, and classical texts associate it with intelligence, good judgement, reputation, eloquence and the support of well-placed people. Its strength depends on Jupiter's and the Moon's dignity and on freedom from affliction or combustion. It describes a tendency, not a guarantee.

entries.title: Budha-Aditya Yoga
entries.body: The Sun and Mercury in the same sign. Classically linked to intellect, skill in work, communication and recognition for learning. Because Mercury is always close to the Sun this is very common, so its weight comes from the house, the dignity of both planets and how deeply Mercury is combust. A combust Mercury shifts the emphasis from brilliance to effort.

entries.title: Chandra-Mangala Yoga
entries.body: The Moon and Mars in the same sign. Traditionally a wealth yoga: enterprise, the drive to earn, and resourcefulness in trade or property. The same pairing can make emotions quick and fiery. Its results improve when the sign and house are supportive and the pair is aspected by benefics.

entries.title: Ruchaka Mahapurusha Yoga
entries.body: Mars in its own sign (Mesha, Vrishchika) or exaltation (Makara) in a kendra from the ascendant. It is one of the five Mahapurusha yogas and is associated with courage, physical strength, leadership in action and success in fields such as the military, sport, engineering or command. Mars's intensity also calls for discipline.

entries.title: Bhadra Mahapurusha Yoga
entries.body: Mercury in its own sign (Mithuna, Kanya) or exaltation (Kanya) in a kendra from the ascendant. It is associated with intelligence, eloquence, skill in trade, learning and a youthful, adaptable nature. Communication, analysis and commerce are its natural fields.

entries.title: Hamsa Mahapurusha Yoga
entries.body: Jupiter in its own sign (Dhanu, Meena) or exaltation (Karka) in a kendra from the ascendant. It is associated with wisdom, righteousness, respect from others, a spiritual disposition and good fortune. Teaching, counsel and dharma-oriented work suit it.

entries.title: Malavya Mahapurusha Yoga
entries.body: Venus in its own sign (Vrishabha, Tula) or exaltation (Meena) in a kendra from the ascendant. It is associated with charm, refinement, artistic talent, comfort, vehicles and happiness in relationships. The caution is indulgence.

entries.title: Sasa Mahapurusha Yoga
entries.body: Saturn in its own sign (Makara, Kumbha) or exaltation (Tula) in a kendra from the ascendant. It is associated with authority gained through perseverance, organisational power, leadership of groups and endurance. Results tend to mature with age.

entries.title: Raja Yoga (kendra-trikona)
entries.body: An association between the lord of a kendra (1, 4, 7, 10), representing effort and position, and the lord of a trikona (1, 5, 9), representing merit and fortune. Classically this promises rise in status and influence, especially during the dashas of the planets involved. Strength depends on their dignity and on whether they also rule difficult houses.

entries.title: Dhana Yoga
entries.body: An association between lords of the wealth houses (2, 5, 9, 11). Tradition reads accumulation of resources and gains through the areas those houses govern, most noticeable in the relevant dashas. Afflictions or dusthana involvement reduce or delay the results.

entries.title: Vipreet Raja Yoga
entries.body: The lord of a dusthana (6, 8, 12) placed in a dusthana. The 'reversed' raja yoga describes gains that emerge from difficulty: success after setbacks, rising when rivals fall, or strength found in crisis. Its results often come suddenly and after a period of challenge.

entries.title: Adhi Yoga
entries.body: Natural benefics (Mercury, Jupiter, Venus) in the 6th, 7th or 8th from the Moon. Classical texts associate it with leadership, comfort, victory over opponents and good health, graded by how many benefics take part and how strong they are. Its protective support is felt through the mind and the social position.

entries.title: Sunapha Yoga
entries.body: Planets other than the Sun in the 2nd from the Moon. It is linked to self-earned wealth, intelligence and a good reputation. The planets forming it colour the result: Mars adds enterprise, Mercury skill, Jupiter virtue, Venus comfort and Saturn endurance.

entries.title: Anapha Yoga
entries.body: Planets other than the Sun in the 12th from the Moon. It is associated with good health, self-control, a dignified presence and contentment. The planets forming it colour its expression, and inner resources are its hallmark.

entries.title: Durudhara Yoga
entries.body: Planets other than the Sun on both sides of the Moon, in the 2nd and the 12th. Traditionally it combines the qualities of Sunapha and Anapha: comforts, wealth, generosity and support around the person. A mind supported from both sides is its core image.

entries.title: Kemadruma Yoga
entries.body: No planets other than the Sun in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon, and none in a kendra from it. Classically a caution about loneliness, fluctuating resources or emotional isolation. Many cancellations are recognised: planets in kendras from the lagna or Moon, a strong or aspected Moon, and benefics in upachayas. Read it as a call to build support, never as a sentence.

entries.title: Neecha Bhanga Raja Yoga
entries.body: The cancellation of a planet's debilitation, for example when the lord of its sign of fall or of its exaltation sign occupies a kendra. Classical texts read this as turning weakness into strength: a start marked by struggle that later yields notable success in the planet's significations.

entries.title: Kala Sarpa (pattern)
entries.body: All seven planets lie on one side of the Rahu–Ketu axis. It is not described in BPHS itself and comes from later tradition. It is read as a life of concentrated, sometimes uneven intensity, with periods of striving followed by breakthroughs. Its weight depends on the full chart, so it should not be treated as a stand-alone affliction.
